whatWasBuilt.theOneProductChange: src/lib/multiplayer/server/MatchRecovery.ts. The `journal.kind === 'journal'` arm no longer returns early into registerRecoveredHost. It falls through into the same checkpointRecoveryPort block the legacy arm uses, via three edits: (1) the early-return block at the pre-change lines 240-248 is deleted and replaced by a comment naming the four properties it used to jump; (2) headRevision is taken from journal.headRevision when the consult answered `journal`, and otherwise still derived from the log's last sequence behind the existing `cache !== null` guard; (3) `read` became async and applies the journal head as a CEILING on top of the one `store.getEvents(matchId, fromExclusive)` call, which is the same read the legacy arm already made.
whatWasBuilt.whyOneStoreReadRatherThanReusingJournalE: The deleted arm folded `journal.events`, and using that array as the port's read source would have placed a SECOND expression of the sequence/revision offset (`revisionForMatchSequence(e.sequence) > fromExclusive`) beside the store read's own exclusive-bound convention. That offset already has named helpers precisely because it was once duplicated inline at several sites (history/matchStoreBranchSegmentReader.ts:53-73, whose doc block says so). Keeping one store read means the exclusive bound lives in exactly one place for both arms, and it is what makes the door test's `[[MATCH_ID, 4]]` tail assertion byte-identical on both arms. The head ceiling is carried explicitly instead, mirroring the consult's own bound at MatchRecoveryJournalHead.ts:127-129.
whatWasBuilt.fileDeliberatelyNotTouched: MatchRecoveryJournalHead.ts needed no change: the consult already carries `headRevision` on its `journal` variant (MatchRecoveryJournalHead.ts:58-67), which is the only extra information checkpointRecoveryPort needed. The brief listed that file conditionally ('if the journal arm's return shape needs to carry more information'); it does not.

perPropertyTable.mapsOntoJournalHeadSemantics: YES. The events the journal arm validates are the MATCH LOG's own rows - the consult reads them with `store.getEvents(matchId, 0)` and only BOUNDS them by the head - so `integrityOf`'s `receiptId: event.id` describes the same data on both arms. The divergence gate recovers only the sequence-continuity half (count plus max revision together force {0..N-1}); two events sharing an id at distinct sequences pass it untouched, which is exactly what S4-R4 said.

perPropertyTable.outcome: ROUTED, with the explicit per-property re-justification S4-R4 asked for recorded below. No semantics were invented.
perPropertyTable.mapsOntoJournalHeadSemantics: YES, and the brief's worry ('quarantine's sequence-gap / broken-lineage / duplicate-receipt vocabulary may not map 1:1 onto journal-head semantics') does not bite - for a reason that is a code fact rather than a judgement. The journal arm does not validate JOURNAL rows at all. It validates the same `mp_match_events` rows the legacy arm validates (MatchRecoveryJournalHead.ts:104), with the head used only as a ceiling and a revision. So `sequence-gap` and `duplicate-receipt` mean on this arm exactly what they mean on the legacy arm, and `broken-lineage` / `missing-digest` are skipped on BOTH arms alike for the same reason: a match log carries no digests, and AuthorityQuarantine.ts:92-95 skips the digest/lineage pass entirely when no event carries one. Quarantine is therefore not a legacy-log-only vocabulary here; it is a MATCH-LOG vocabulary, and both arms read the match log.
citations: AuthorityQuarantine.ts:157-162 QUARANTINABLE = sequence-gap | broken-lineage | duplicate-receipt | missing-digest; :164-169 isCorruptionReason; :181-194 quarantineAuthorityCorruption.

AuthorityQuarantine.ts:92-95 `if (!events.some((event) => event.digest !== null)) return null;` - the digest and lineage checks are conditional on the authority carrying digests, and the match authority declares `previousDigest: null, digest: null`.
MatchRecovery.ts `quarantineAuthorityCorruption(quarantine, { authorityType: 'match', authorityId: meta.matchId }, verdict)` inside the blocked arm - line unchanged, now reached by both arms.

perPropertyTable.whatWasDeliberatelyNotRouted: The consult's `diverged` verdict still blocks WITHOUT quarantining - the `partial-history` arm of MatchRecovery.ts is unchanged, comment included ('a mirror that fell behind is a desynchronized copy, not authority data that is wrong, and quarantineAuthorityCorruption draws that same line'). That is the one journal-SIDE corruption shape that exists today. Making it quarantinable would contradict both that comment and MatchRecoveryJournalHead.ts:33-40, which states the same line independently. Recorded as owner question OQ-1 rather than changed.

perPropertyTable.mapsOntoJournalHeadSemantics: YES, directly - and the journal head is a better `headRevision` than the log-derived one because it is stated rather than re-derived. On this arm the two agree by construction (the consult refuses `diverged` otherwise), so the refresh records at the same revision the legacy arm would have, without a second derivation of the offset.

Two independent places already state the line in prose - MatchRecovery.ts's partial-history comment and MatchRecoveryJournalHead.ts:33-40 - and both say a mirror that fell behind is a desynchronized copy rather than authority data that is wrong. Reversing it means revisiting that line, which is an owner call and not an implementer's.
